(a) Notice that we must have f(x) < f (sup A), because f is continuous at
sup A and there are points y arbitrarily close to sup A with f(x) < f(y).
(A simple 2-5 argument is being suppressed.) Now suppose that sup A < b.
Then f(b) < f(x). Moreover, sup A is a shadow point, so there is some
2> sup A with f(z) > f(sup A) > f(x). We cannot have z < b, for this
would mean that z isin A. Soz > band f(b) < f(x) < f(z), contradicting
the fact that b is not a shadow point.
(b) Since f is continuous at a, and f(x) < f(b) forall x in (a, b), it follows
that f(x) < f(b) (either by a simple £-3 argument, or using Problem 8-6, if
you prefer).
